questions.def: 'Later' refers to a time after the point already mentioned.
questions.question: It wasn't until ___ that I understood the problem.

questions.def: After 'not only', the auxiliary verb comes before the subject.
questions.question: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot his presentation.

questions.def: Past simple to show the report did this at a specific time.
questions.question: The report ___ the importance of early detection.

questions.def: The subject 'what I need' is singular, so use 'is'.
questions.question: What I need ___ a good night's sleep.

questions.def: 'Who' refers to people (the manager).
questions.question: It is the manager ___ is responsible for this decision.

questions.def: Present simple shows a fact about the article.
questions.question: The article ___ the challenges faced by young entrepreneurs.

questions.def: 'All that' introduces the desired thing.
questions.question: All ___ I want is to travel the world.

questions.def: 'So + adjective/adverb + auxiliary verb...' is the structure.
questions.question: So ___ did he study that he passed with flying colors.

questions.def: Past simple to show a specific event in the past.
questions.question: The manager ___ the importance of teamwork.

questions.def: It was + place + that + clause (focus on place).
questions.question: It was in Paris ___ I first met her.

questions.def: 'Not until then' refers to a specific time after.
questions.question: Not until ___ did I feel confident.

questions.def: Past simple: a completed action in the past.
questions.question: The professor ___ the key concepts in red.

questions.def: Adverb 'vitally' modifies the adjective 'important'.
questions.question: It is ___ important to submit your work on time.

questions.def: Inversion after 'little': Little did I know...
questions.question: Little ___ I know that the project would fail.

questions.def: Present simple: a fact about the report.
questions.question: The report ___ the need for further investment.

questions.def: 'It was ... that' is used to emphasize a specific noun.
questions.question: It was the rain ___ caused the flooding.

questions.def: 'Only after' introduces the timing of the realization.
questions.question: Only ___ the exam, he realised his mistakes.

questions.def: Base form after 'to' (to stress).
questions.question: I want to ___ how important this is.

questions.def: Singular subject 'what I appreciate' takes singular verb 'is'.
questions.question: What I appreciate ___ her dedication.

questions.def: 'It is precisely this...' emphasizes the problem.
questions.question: It is precisely ___ that makes this problem so difficult.

questions.def: Past simple: the speech did this at a specific time.
questions.question: The speech ___ the importance of education.

questions.def: Inversion after rarely requires auxiliary 'have'.
questions.question: Rarely ___ I been so impressed with a presentation.

questions.def: Singular subject 'what surprised me' requires singular verb 'was'.
questions.question: What surprised me ___ the level of commitment.

questions.def: 'Not until' requires 'later' to express a delayed realization.
questions.question: It wasn't until ___ I understood the problem.

questions.def: 'All' is used to emphasize the entirety of one's desire.
questions.question: ___ I want is a little peace and quiet.

questions.def: The sentence needs a simple past tense for a completed action.
questions.question: The report ___ the need for immediate action.

questions.def: 'Once' clearly establishes the completion before the next action.
questions.question: ___ she had finished, she went to bed.

questions.def: 'It was' emphasizes the surprising nature of his words.
questions.question: ___ what he said surprised everyone.

questions.def: The sentence needs the base form of the verb after 'to'.
questions.question: I want to ___ the importance of this issue.

questions.def: 'Not only...but also' is the correct correlative conjunction.
questions.question: Not ___ did he forget his keys, but also his wallet.
